methodological_rigor.justification: A retrospective single-center cohort of 79 gastric adenocarcinoma patients is used to define sarcopenia via TPAI combined with SARC-F and dynamometry under EWGSOP2 criteria. Major methodological concern is that TPAI cutoffs (6.04 men, 4.98 women) were derived in the same cohort via ROC using mortality as the outcome and the Youden index, then used in the survival analyses; this is circular and overfits the cutoff to the outcome. The authors acknowledge this risk but still build subsequent univariate/multivariate Cox models on the derived binary variable without cross-validation or bootstrap. Sample size and event count are small for Cox multivariable adjustment (only 24 deaths), raising the risk of overfitting with multiple covariates (age, sex, tumor stage). The reported OS mean of 43.7 months (95% CI 42.6-44.8) with 18-month median follow-up is inconsistent with a median follow-up so short, suggesting reporting issues. No sensitivity or external validation is performed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort maps to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is moderate: preoperative CT-derived sarcopenia markers are clinically accessible since CT is routine for staging, and integration with strength and SARC-F extends the conventional imaging-only approach. However, the proposed cutoffs are not externally validated, so immediate practice change is unwarranted; the work informs risk stratification and prehabilitation research rather than guidelines.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the closest applicable standard because this is a prognostic-biomarker study using TPAI. The manuscript reports ethics approval (CEIm PI 2025 02 1832), R and package versions, clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, and clinical outcomes (Clavien-Dindo, CCI). However, REMARK-specific items are incomplete: no STARD/REMARK checklist, limited reporting of how the cutoff was internally validated, no reporting of assay reproducibility (measurement agreement for TPA), and insufficient details on missing-data handling. No data/code deposit is described. Some numerical inconsistencies appear (e.g., NSG 64.6% vs 36.7% SG sums to 101.3%, and Figure 3 is described twice with different p-values 0.0042 and 0.0055).

novelty_literature.justification: The prognostic role of low psoas/skeletal muscle mass in gastric cancer has been widely reported (cited refs 5, 10, 11, 12, 31). The additional contribution here is the combined EWGSOP2-compliant assessment (muscle mass + strength + SARC-F) and proposed cohort-specific cutoffs, but this is incremental confirmation rather than a new concept or method. Guarded against leniency, novelty is limited because EWGSOP2 integration in cancer surgery cohorts is already established and cohort-specific cutoffs without external validation add little generalizable knowledge.

writing_presentation.justification: Structure is adequate and the manuscript is readable, but there are multiple internal inconsistencies and minor errors: 64.6% + 36.7% = 101.3% for sarcopenia classification; mean OS 43.7 months (CI 42.6-44.8) with 18-month median follow-up and 30% mortality is statistically implausible and poorly explained; the discussion reports p=0.0042 and p=0.0055 for the same DFS/OS Kaplan-Meier comparison; a Cox analysis paragraph is duplicated; and references 23 and 27 (pROC) appear misaligned. Tables are referenced but numerical summaries are repeated awkwardly in prose.

key_strengths: Uses EWGSOP2-compliant multimodal definition of sarcopenia (TPAI + handgrip dynamometry + SARC-F) rather than imaging-only
Provides longitudinal TPAI measurements at pre-op, 6, and 12 months, adding descriptive temporal data
Standardized outcome reporting with Clavien-Dindo, CCI, and explicit R package versions
Multivariable Cox model reported with HRs and 95% CIs for sarcopenia (HR 1.8; 1.1-3.2) and advanced stage (HR 2.5; 1.4-4.5)
key_concerns: TPAI cutoffs derived on the same cohort using mortality as the outcome (ROC/Youden), then used in subsequent survival analyses - a classic overfitting concern acknowledged only briefly
Small sample size (n=79) with limited death events makes multivariable Cox unstable and confidence intervals wide

Internal inconsistencies: sarcopenia proportions sum to >100%, mean OS 43.7 months incompatible with 18-month median follow-up, duplicated paragraphs and conflicting p-values (0.0042 vs 0.0055) for the same figures
Novelty is limited because prognostic value of low psoas/muscle mass in gastric cancer is already well documented
No external validation, no data/code availability, and REMARK checklist items are incompletely addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: A small retrospective prognostic biomarker study with circular cutoff derivation and multiple internal numerical inconsistencies. Tier 4 is the realistic ceiling, and major revisions are necessary to reconcile numbers, perform proper internal or external validation of the cutoff, and fix duplicated text.
